video.title: The Abdominal Corkscrew ft. Carson Branstine

classification.reason: The coach provides an actionable drill at the end of the video where the player takes a wide stance and drives the knee to the elbow on the side of the body to feel abdominal tension.

problem.title_as_question: How do you generate easy, effortless power in limited time using the abdominal corkscrew?
problem.definition: Players often misunderstand hip drive and try to time millisecond-level hip-shoulder separation consciously, leading to a disconnected swing rather than tapping into effortless power generated by stretching and uncoiling the abdomen.
prerequisites: coiling upper body relative to hips

quotes.text: The reason I call her power easy or effortless, is because of points like this, which they don't look as flashy as winners.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Now, the secret to this easy, effortless power is in the abdomen.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: you can see in the skin on her abdomen that her trunk, her shoulder line, her chest, it is twisted back farther than her hips.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: The first thing I want you to notice is that the trunk is moving faster than the hips for pretty much the entire swing.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: So that's number one is you know a lot of people get the idea of hip drive into their mind and that's amazing except it must be connected to the trunk through that tension in the abdomen.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: If your hips are going by themselves, then your swing is actually getting discombobulated and you're losing that tension corkcrew coil that she's recruiting through the abdomen here.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Now biomechanically the hips, the pelvis, it actually moves faster than the trunk for about 25 milliseconds. But you're not going to be able to feel that.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: I want you to aim for that feeling of tension and power in your abdomen rather than thinking about the timing windows because the timing windows are too small for you to actually feel.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: That shoulder line, that upper part of the trunk really needs to yank itself out and participate in that explosive twist.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: So the purpose of the hips is to speed up the trunk. And then of course the purpose of the trunk is to speed up the arm.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Her mastery over the abdominal corkcrew everywhere around the court is the only reason she was able to compete with Arena Sabalanka in that second set.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: We see that abdomen is stretched in the back. That tension between the upper part of the thorax and the hips.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Very important not to overfocus on your hips from a sensory perspective because right away the trunk is going with the hips.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And so you want to perceive that sensation of that shoulder line, your chest, your trunk firing around.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Depending on the shot you're playing, you can wind up more or less. you can load more or less power into your trunk and hips and make that power control trade-off shot by shot as you see fit.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And lastly, I want to give you a drill that we use with our clients all the time to help them feel this tension and this corkcrew because it can be kind of difficult to feel if you've never felt
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: You get in a nice wide stance and you drive your knee to the elbow on the side of your body like this.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And this is going to help you feel that tension and you're going to be able to explode faster and harder and faster and harder as you start to feel that sensation your abdomen
quotes.speaker: coach

symptoms.description: The swing becomes discombobulated with hips firing by themselves without connected trunk velocity.
Lack of effortless pace and inability to hit powerful strikes in limited time.
Inability to feel stretch tension or corkscrew recruit in the abdomen during load and forward swing.

causes.statement: The trunk is not twisted back farther than the hips in the load position to create abdominal stretch tension.
The hips drive in isolation without being mechanically connected to the trunk through abdominal tension.
Players try to cognitively manage 25-millisecond hip-shoulder separation timing windows rather than targeting somatic abdominal stretch tension.
The upper trunk and front shoulder get left behind instead of actively pulling forward into the explosive twist.

angles.summary: The hips accelerate the trunk via abdominal stretch tension, which in turn accelerates the arm, with trunk rotating faster than hips throughout the swing.
Players should focus on sensing tension and coiling in the abdominal fascia and muscles rather than micro-timing hip leads.
The unwinding abdominal tension acts as a slingshot, flinging the trunk forward past the hips.
The idea of hip drive leads players to fire hips by themselves, which discombobulates the kinetic chain if unconnected to the trunk.
Carson Branstine and Carlos Alcaraz vary their abdominal corkscrew coil depending on the incoming ball to trade off effortless power and control.

solutions.summary: Aim for the sensation of stretch tension and power in your abdomen rather than attempting to consciously time hip-shoulder separation.
Perceive the shoulder line, chest, and trunk firing around together with hip drive rather than overfocusing sensorially on the hips.
Modulate the abdominal corkscrew wind-up dynamically shot by shot, coiling less on fast incoming balls and coiling maximum on floaters.
Stand in a wide stance and drive your knee to the elbow on the same side of your body to recruit and feel abdominal corkscrew tension.
solutions.external_goal: Touch or bring knee towards elbow on the side of the body
